prompt: Two people study for three hours each. Who tends to remember more weeks later?

options.text: The one who split it into sessions over several days
The one who crammed it all the night before

explanation: That is the spacing effect: with the same total time, spread-out sessions produce longer-lasting memories.
misconception: Cramming can work for the next day’s test, but the memory fades much faster.

prompt: According to one common explanation, why does spacing out study help?

options.text: Forgetting a little forces the brain to rebuild the memory, which strengthens it
The brain only stores memories at night
Short sessions are easier on the eyes

explanation: The effort of retrieving something you have started to forget seems to strengthen memory more than reviewing something still fresh.
